quest.title: Alan Smithee, Author of Fischl
quest.description: You only stopped by the Adventurers' Guild to check for new commissions — it has nothing to do with the witch or her assignment. But it seems you stumble upon an unexpected surprise...
quest.rewards_formatted: Hero's Wit x3, Guide to Ballad x3, Mora x30000

talks.objective: Go to the Adventurers' Guild in Mondstadt

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #Ad astra abyssosque. Greetings, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Katheryne! Oh, and Oz and Fischl are here too! What a coincidence!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: All things in this universe must plunge into darkness. 'Tis only natural that those who seek light should cross paths in the realm of dawn.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: #Mein Fräulein means to say, she's happy to see you both. And I feel the same. It's been quite a while, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #You're here just in time. Yae Publishing House has a commission for you, {NICKNAME}. An editor is here to discuss the details in person.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Much of the information was kept from the Guild for business reasons. All we know is that it has something to do with the author of the "Legend of the Shattered Halberd"...

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: What? Surely you don't mean...!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: *clears throat*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is this author really that important? What if we weren't here, or if we decided not to take the commission... The editor would just be wasting their time!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: In that case, it'd be a free trip to Mondstadt where one needs only pass some information along... That's an opportunity most would fight over.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: In any case, if the commission is of interest to you, the editor is waiting at the Good Hunter. Just look for the man dressed in Inazuman clothing.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Hold on... I mean, halt thy steps, good Traveler. Fate casts you upon the tides of the world, but not for you to stand alone in the face of its desolation...

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Nay — you step forth onto the path of the Immernachtreich!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: What Mein Fräulein means to say is, she would like to go with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fischl seems really jazzed about this commission. Do you think she has some kind of insider information?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're welcome to come along, either way.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Well, let's head to the Good Hunter to meet with this editor, then.

talks.objective: Go to the Good Hunter to find the editor who's here to make contact

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's see who lucked out and got this free trip to Mondstadt...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you're Xing— Uh, Zhenyu's editor, Onodera!

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, thank you for all you've done for us in the past. I come here today with a commission from Lady Yae, with which I'd like your help, should you be willing...

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Oh, and might I ask who this person dressed like Princess Fischl is?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: You have the pleasure of speaking to our eminent person. Fischl, Prinzessin der Verurteilung.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein means to say that her name is Fischl, and that she is most pleased to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, this is Fischl. She's a reliable adventurer, and she's here to help!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right. This is Fischl.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Y—Yeah, I, uh, kinda got that the first time.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Since thou hast learned my name, understand this. To speak it is to be absolved. Praise it, therefore, and thou shalt earn thine salvation.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein means to say, she—

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. I completely concur, milady. Remembering names is simply basic etiquette. And if you might lend me succor in solving this problem, I shall indeed praise your name to the heavens above. As many times as necessary, in fact!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You understood Fischl language before Oz could even finish translating!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: An editor is not to be underestimated.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Well, let's get down to brass tacks, then.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Now, have you heard of the author, Mr. Nine? He's famous for writing the "Legend of the Shattered Halberd."

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Flowers...

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: What was that, Mein Fräulein?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Flowers for Princess Fischl. That's what Mr. Nine is actually famous for!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Ahem, Mein Fräulein means to say, even should the Creator be but cold and unmoving, the Prinzessin and her Immernachtreich's resplendence might yet compel them to weep.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Well, sure. The author of "Flowers for Princess Fischl," Mr. Nine... He sent a letter from Nod-Krai asking for help, and he seems to be in bad shape.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, so ask the Adventurers' Guild or a local mercenary to find him. Seems pretty simple to Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Were it so simple. But here's the problem. We don't know anything about Mr. Nine — what he looks like, how old he is, where he's from...

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: He's only ever communicated with us via letter, from addresses all over Teyvat. And he's never showed up to our annual meeting or events — not once.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what are we supposed to do?

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Well, we'll need to investigate Mr. Nine's identity, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: We did a bit of digging ourselves, and we realized that, ever since completing the "Shattered Halberd" series, Mr. Nine's handwriting began to change.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: His initial editor has decided to retire to focus on his own writing, and he didn't have much to add either.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Whatever hath once existed in this world is enshrined in the memory of the Prinzessin der Verurteilung, to endure unchanging in her Immernachtreich. For from the sacred primordial words flow the wellspring of all cause and consequence.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein means to say that—

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Yes, we had the same idea. So, we tracked down the original manuscript of the "Legend of the Shattered Halberd"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, man. Xing— Um, Zhenyu's gonna be so mad he missed out on this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you didn't need Oz to translate this time either, Onodera!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Editors are somethin' else.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Ozvaldo Hrafnavins, hast thou perceived something?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: No such "Henry" exists, Mein Fräulein.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: I sense a faint, elusive resonance. Something akin to the... magnetic field, gravitational force, and threads of cause and effect that surround you, Mein Fräulein.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Isn't that interesting... Well, in the end, our only takeaway was that the design and craftsmanship of the paper point to it coming from Qingce Village in Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Could Mr. Nine be from Liyue, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, wait. If we're talking authors from Qingce Village, specifically...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Chang the Ninth?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, it couldn't be... Could it?

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Chang the Ninth? Ah, I've heard of him. He won a best new author award for the "First Apprentice of Guhua."

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: It matters not. Though the Saint of Tears and Saint of Atonement perform manifold labors on divergent principles, their power flows but from a single source.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mr. Onodera, if you please...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Oz! It's great that you trust Onodera and all, but we're still in the dark over here!

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: You speak true, Mein Prinzessin. Even if Chang the Ninth doesn't turn out to be Mr. Nine, he's still an author, and he could have had contact with him. I think it's a good place to start.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What did I tell you. Editors... am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Well, either way, I appreciate the help! I'm counting on you!

talks.objective: Head to Qingce Village and ask Chang the Ninth for details

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Chang the Ninth isn't home.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: It doesn't look like there's anyone around we can ask, either. Shall we wait?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like that's all we can do.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Still, could his absence mean that... he really is Mr. Nine, now kidnapped and sent to Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Perhaps we should have a look around his house...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Barging in without permission seems wrong, but if he really is Mr. Nine, then... Okay, let's do it.

talks.objective: Investigate the clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there anything else we should know about Mr. Nine?

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Well, according to some reader Q&As and his author's notes, he has a receding hairline, a slight pot belly, he doesn't like sweet things, and his heart is on the right side...

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Or was it the left? No, it was the right. He has five fingers on his left hand, severe insomnia, a pupil in each eye...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... a whole bunch of nothing.

talks.objective: Investigate the clues in the area
Investigate the clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just seems like a bunch of ordinary stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Nay. I, the Prinzessin, have beheld the mystery of the universe enshrined in these specks of dust. What hath been revealed... is the very fount of wisdom. Ever does it flow toward the shores of truth.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein means to say, she thinks this is a clue.

talks.objective: Investigate the location that caught Fischl's attention

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Fancying myself to be Mr. Nine, you say... You know, that might just expand my creative horizons.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Alright. Now, uh, what would he write...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, it looks like the soil's been overturned!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, could some kind of overzealous fan have buried him in here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Maybe we should call the Millelith. What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: It's alright, Paimon. Mr. Nine's most zealous fan happens to be right here.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: And since Mein Fräulein would never do anyone harm, I'm certain the same is true of his other, less avid supporters.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright, let's see what's buried here in any case.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
You dig up the ground. 
 Inside, you find a large bag of Mora and a check from the Northland Bank...

 Suddenly, a voice comes out of nowhere, and without thinking, you stuff the items into your pocket.
What is the meaning of this! I'm calling the Millelith!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chang the Ninth! You're not dead! Or kidnapped!

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: What are you even talking abou— Wait a second... You're the ones who came here with that young lad from the Guhua clan. Yes, I remember.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Hmm. I'm guessing this is a misunderstanding, then. The question still stands, though... What are you doing digging around my house?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, well, um... Actually, we just wanted to know if you've ever written under the pen name "Mr. Nine."

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: What? Haha. Not even a whole bucket of hallucinogenic mushrooms could make me that delusional. No, no. If I were Mr. Nine, why in the world would I enter all those writing competitions?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: To, what? Demolish the competition from the shadows? Yes... Doing a real bang up job, aren't I? My submission's never even been selected...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: The classic archetype of the boy-hero is outdated. That's the kind of critique I get. "Even opening with a plot twist or disguising your hero as a fool is falling out of fashion."

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: ...Modern readers are drawn to the boundless imagination and innovative world-building character of Mr. Nine's works.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good point.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Besides, if I were Mr. Nine, I would've come clean the minute "First Apprentice of Guhua" won that award.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: "What? That old, beggarly Chang the Ninth is Mr. Nine? No, there must be some mistake... Heh, what a sight that would've been."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, and when we were here with Xingqiu that one time, you talked up the "Legend of the Shattered Halberd" a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you were the one who wrote it, that'd be like... Jean complimenting herself for being a good Knight. It just doesn't add up.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: In any case, while this gentleman isn't the Mr. Nine we're looking for, I sense something of interest on his person.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: It's a peculiar signature — the same threads of "fate" I sensed on you, Mein Fräulein, and on the manuscript. I believe the traces are related to Mr. Nine, and it appears I can... track them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, that's perfect! Once we head to Nod-Krai, you should be able to find Mr. Nine no problem, then!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, back to the "signature"... What were you doing before this, Chang the Ninth?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Oh, well, I ran out of manuscript paper, so I went to buy some. I'm particular about that kind of thing — the creation of literature demands the highest quality.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Ah, no wonder. Mr. Nine uses the very same type for his manuscripts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that explains it! Thanks, Chang the Ninth. We should get going!

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I'm not quite sure what I did, but... You're welcome, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Farewell, creator of another world — though I must say, the laws and narratives thou hast ordained can scarce compare to the dream-dust sedimented in the Immernachtreich.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein means to say, your writing isn't... Ahem, I mean, Mein Fräulein offers her thanks.

talks.objective: Go to Nod-Krai and search for Mr. Nine with Oz
Go to Nod-Krai and search for Mr. Nine with Oz

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: It should be up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, did something attack that Seelie? Something doesn't seem right here.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Hmm, and it bears the same signature I sensed before.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Then it would seem fate has dictated our path for us.

talks.objective: Go to Nod-Krai and search for Mr. Nine with Oz

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, looks like this Seelie is showing us the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's follow.

talks.objective: Talk to the person behind the scenes
Talk to the person behind the scenes

dialogues.text: Hmm? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that voice... It's Nicole!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, that should be our line! We were looking for Mr. Nine, and our search led us here, but now it seems we've found you instead.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Nicole and the Seelie about Yae Publishing House's commission and your investigation...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. Well, "Mr." Nine... is right here.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: Hello!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Wh—What bizarre Dämmerung is this? Never in a thousand sunsets have I heard of such a thing!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: In truth, I too aspire to be an author, but I'm also partial to direct communication — talking is rather inconvenient by comparison.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: And, as I'm sure you can understand, writing things down is even more tedious.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I thought, perhaps, if I found someone with whom I could share my ideas, it might give me the same release as writing. But then, those stories would never see the light of day, which would be a shame...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: So, I tracked down an old Seelie friend of mine, and told her all the stories I was imagining. Then, I sent her to find people with similar aspirations to write them in my stead.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: We even came up with several character traits to lend a certain "authenticity" to Mr. Nine. A receding hair line was one of them, I think...

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: Yep. I'm the one she roped into all this.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Come now. It was beneficial for you, too. By inhabiting those authors and mobilizing their language faculties, you were able to hone, and eventually recover, your capacity for speech.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: And anyway, an angel has always functioned like a sort of... flash of inspiration in someone's head. I'm sure it was like stepping into old shoes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you, what? Possessed people? Isn't that kinda... intrusive?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, it's fine. She did it while they were sleeping.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: As long as the person is someone who dreams of creating worlds of their own, this "inner writer" within them will automatically awaken.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, that sounds very "automatic."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but... What about the letter and the strange intuitions Oz has been having?

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: Nicole sent me to monitor the situation in Nod-Krai, and it's super dangerous, okay? So, I needed some help. It's not like I have the knowledge or power of the heavens anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: As for your friend over here... Well, you see, when writing a story, it's not uncommon to incorporate certain... half-true details. For realism's sake, you understand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we've seen that before. A real curse was written into an Inazuman light novel once...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Indeed. In a similar vein, "Mr." Nine's stories are full of metaphors, including one for the creation of life. What it describes isn't made-up, per se...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: We just never imagined someone would actually manage to use it... until you came along, young lady.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein is speechless. So, if I may ask in her stead... did she manage to use one of these "half-truths" in Mr. Nine's novels to create me?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It was more like... 70 percent made-up, 30 percent true.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: No, it was 90 percent made-up, 10 percent true. I thought it was too dangerous, so I changed it. See, I knew you'd never read my books!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't seem too surprised, Oz...

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Well... I suppose I've vaguely sensed this since the beginning. Regardless, it is an honor to serve Mein Fräulein.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well, once our affairs in Nod-Krai are resolved, "Mr." Nine will be able to return home. Yes, just tell them that when you return.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: Ugh! I don't want to be your eyes here! It's too dangerous!

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: Oh, but, uh... While you're at it, could you pass a message along to that guy in Qingce Village? I've been splitting the royalties with him 90-10 — his share's been buried in his yard all these years.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what do you use the Mora for?

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: I bury it and then lead people to the treasure. Guiding people is in our nature. It's what I love to do.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: Feel free to come search for my personal stash someday. I've buried it at the furthest end of the Immernachtreich.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: I will! I absolutely will!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: And, um... I just want to say that... I really like your books, Mr. Nine!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: What Mein Fräulein means is, though the cosmos stretch forth in unending darkness, yet shall come an hour when all things shine.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: I'm glad to hear it. All in all, it seems you've already found my greatest treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alright, that settles that. Now, I need to have a quick argument with "Mr." Nine about who really deserves to be considered first author.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shouldn't it be Chang the Ninth?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole & Fischl & Mr. Nine
dialogues.text: Absolutely not.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After saying your goodbyes, you begin the return journey.
